points: Worked in a simulated startup environment and picked a real problem: robot vacuums can't get between floors.
Prototyped an Arduino-controlled stair-climbing mechanism, taking a $1,000 stair-climbing Roomba down to about $100 in parts for a regular Roomba.

points: Built a Kafka and FastAPI pipeline that segments 2GB+ whole-slide kidney images in under 5 minutes each.
Trained U-Net models that turn tissue into binary masks of tubules and their basement membrane, automating annotation that took pathologists hours per slide.

points: Co-manage the largest student-run makerspace in the US, with 500+ tools serving 1,000+ users.
Train students on waterjet, laser cutting, 3D printing and machining, and help makers pick how to build their projects.

points: Connected a Chi.Bio bioreactor to a real-time flow cytometer, so bacteria are pumped and analyzed continuously instead of hand-loaded by syringe.
Showed the bioreactor grows cultures as well as a standard incubator.
Parallelized alginate gel generation for gastruloid culture: 10 capillaries made about 11,000 gels in 5 minutes versus about 1,200 with one, then designed a microdevice to make the setup easy.

points: Architected a data ingestion pipeline used internally by 10+ scientists, cutting ingestion time from a day to minutes.
